item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00471","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C23","C24"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 is a concrete and material drafting template for the child. Both proclamations invoke the same version of section 22, proceed through the same sequence of Agriculture advice, Tariff Commission investigation and report, presidential findings of interference with a price-support program, necessity of quantitative limits, and an operative import quota. Most decisively, the child reproduces C02's detailed seed exception—including the 100-bushel threshold, approval-or-bond mechanism, customs valuation formula, and six-month deadline—while substituting rye and its 56-pound bushel for oats and its 32-pound bushel. C23 and C24 share substantial section 22 quota machinery, but neither matches the child's full structure and specialized seed exception as closely.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the Secretary of Agriculture advised me there was reason to believe that rye, rye flour, and rye meal are being or are practically certain to be imported ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the price-support program","parent_excerpt":"the Secretary of Agriculture has advised me that he has reason to believe that oats are being or are practically certain to be imported ... as to render or tend to render ineffective, or materially interfere with, the price-support program","explanation":"Distinctively parallel opening recital under the same statutory authority, adapted from oats to rye."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas, on December 9, 1953, I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation ... Whereas the said Tariff Commission has made such investigation and has reported to me its findings and recommendations","parent_excerpt":"Whereas, on June 6, 1953, I caused the United States Tariff Commission to make an investigation ... Whereas the said Tariff Commission has made such investigation and has reported to me its findings and recommendations","explanation":"The same investigation-and-report sequence appears in virtually identical language."},{"child_excerpt":"The provisions of this proclamation shall not apply to certified or registered seed rye for use for seeding and crop-improvement purposes, in bags tagged and sealed by an officially recognized seed-certifying agency ... if (a) the individual shipment amounts to 100 bushels ... or (b) ... written approval of the Secretary of Agriculture ... or bond is furnished ... equal to the value of the merchandise ... plus the estimated duty ... conditioned upon the production of such written approval within six months","parent_excerpt":"The provisions of this proclamation shall not apply to certified or registered seed oats for use for seeding and crop-improvement purposes, in bags tagged and sealed by an officially recognized seed-certifying agency ... Provided, (a) that the individual shipment amounts to 100 bushels ... or (b) ... written approval of the Secretary of Agriculture ... or bond is furnished ... equal to the value of the merchandise ... plus the estimated duty ... conditioned upon the production of such written approval within 6 months","explanation":"This highly specific exception and bond procedure is reproduced almost verbatim, with only the commodity and bushel weight changed."}]}
